answer: Each agent must stake tokens before its offers count, and a contract can slash that stake when the agent fails a randomly sampled audit of its claimed work. Auditors are selected from independent, staked agents and earn fees only when their verdicts agree with later checks, so a fake identity cannot cheaply manufacture trust by joining a grove or posing as a harbor. An attacker must lock capital for every identity, pay for real work, and risk losing the stake; splitting one reputation across many names multiplies that cost. A vine of linked accounts still has to fund each stake separately.
